subject: Clarifications on Model Risk Evidence Sequence and Regression Plan for Medicorp RFP
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@medicorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@medicorp.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medicorp.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications on Model Risk Evidence Sequence and Regression Plan for Medicorp RFP

Hi Marco / Ellen —

Thanks for sending the RFP and the governance questionnaire. Attached is a concise package that should address the majority of your technical/compliance asks and gives a proposed evidence delivery cadence we can commit to during procurement. Attachments: redwood_eval_architecture_v2.pdf (mapping to NIST AI RMF + EU AI Act), SOC2-summary.pdf (controls summary), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (suggested milestones).

High-level summary:
- Classification: Based on the use cases described in the RFP, we consider the primary surfaces to be "high-impact" under NIST AI RMF for performance monitoring and traceability; EU AI Act applicability will depend on whether the models are used to make solely automated decisions vs. human-in-the-loop workflows. We provide a default high-risk annex we can adopt if your legal team deems the system high-risk.
- Evidence sequence: we propose a three-phase delivery: 1) Baseline architecture + controls (week 0–1), 2) Regression harness + baseline evaluations and sampling plan (week 2–3), 3) Ongoing monitoring configuration + runbook and SLA exceptions (week 4). See redwood_regression_timeline.xlsx for specifics.
- Regression approach: continuous sampling + targeted focused regressions for any model changes, automated metric drift detection (per-model AUROC/accuracy for classification tasks; perplexity + human eval sampling for generative tasks), and an eval suite that ties to your acceptance criteria. We can provide the eval harness (PyTest-style runner) and sample datasets under an MSA confidentiality schedule.

Can you confirm the following so we can finalize the annex:
1) Whether Medicorp will treat the integration as a "high-risk" AI system under the EU AI Act (we can default to high-risk controls if preferred).
2) Which 2–3 API surfaces you want prioritized for regression sampling (suggest: patient-summary generation, physician-assist Q&A, clinical-risk scoring).
3) Any procurement timeline constraints or legal redlines we should be aware of before we upload the final annex.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the attachments and the timeline.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarifications on Model Risk Evidence Sequence and Regression Plan for Medicorp RFP

Grace —

Thanks for the quick package, very helpful. A few clarifying points so our risk and legal teams can scope review:

1) EU AI Act classification: Medicorp's integration will be deployed in EU clinics and used to triage patients in an assisted manner (doctor supervises final decisions). That suggests high-risk labelled systems in our reading, but legal will confirm. If you can provide the specific control mapping (e.g., logging/traceability fields & retention windows, documentation templates) that would speed the review.

2) Regression metrics: can you provide an example list of the evaluation metrics and sample sizes you plan for generative outputs (we're particularly concerned about hallucination rate and critical factuality for medication instructions)? Also: what forensic traceability do you provide (audit logs, per-request model/version id, token-level hashes)?

3) Timeline: our security review needs at least a 10-business-day window for a first pass. Can you confirm the minimal evidence set Redwood can deliver before that review to unblock procurement?

If you can respond in writing and attach the mapping tables we'll circulate internally.

Marco
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Medicorp Health

Also attach our SOC2 summary and a short note on encryption/KMS.

Also include a short paragraph on token-level traceability (hash approach) and availability of per-request model/version ids in audit logs.

Also: what forensic traceability do you provide (audit logs, per-request model/version id, token-level hashes)?
>
> 3) Timeline: our security review needs at least a 10-business-day window for a first pass. Can you confirm the minimal evidence set Redwood can deliver before that review to unblock procurement?

Action items: please review the attached mutual-action-plan.xlsx and redwood_regression_timeline.xlsx and confirm what's deliverable within 7 business days vs. 10. My proposal: baseline architecture + SOC2 summary + control mapping + an example metrics table within 7 business days; full regression harness + sample runs and curated dataset within 10 business days.

Marissa—if legal is comfortable with the proposed minimal evidence set, can we flag any MSA redlines that would delay delivery?

Thanks — I can consolidate into a single annex once you both confirm.

Grace

Marco / Ellen —

Quick follow-up with concrete answers and links; see the attached annex in the Drive (link below) and the minimal evidence set we can deliver within 7 business days to support your security review.

1) EU AI Act classification: given your described deployment (clinician-in-loop triage), we'll treat this as high-risk for the purposes of the annex. The annex documents the additional documentation and controls we supply by default when a deployment is considered high-risk (traceability fields, documentation templates, human oversight patterns).

2) Regression metrics and sample sizes (summary):
- Generative outputs (patient summaries): hallucination rate (measured by presence of unsupported assertions) — baseline target <2% on sampled clinical prompts; factuality checklist sampling (n=500 for initial baseline); BLEU/ROUGE not a primary signal but included where structured outputs exist.
- Safety-critical instructions (medication guidance): we do focused rule-based checks + human-in-the-loop adjudication for any flagged outputs; targeted sample n=1,000 for baseline, with automated alarms for out-of-distribution prompt patterns.
- Traceability: per-request audit logs include request id, API consumer id, model name and immutable model version id, prompt fingerprint (SHA256), response digest, and optionally token-level hashes for forensic inspection. Logs are exportable to your SIEM or retained in our encrypted storage; default retention 90 days, extendable contractually.

3) Minimal evidence set for a 7-business-day deliverable:
- Redacted architecture diagram + control mapping (PDF)
- SOC2 summary (PDF)
- Example eval metrics table + sampling plan (CSV)
- Short regression run summary (sample outputs, n=200)

The full regression harness with 1k+ samples and the curated datasets will follow within 10 business days. Drive link to the annex and evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/redwood-medicorp-evidence (access granted to your pendings list).

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Monday 09/28 at 10:00am CET to review the annex and confirm the MSA redlines. Does that work for your team?

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
